message.content: In Christian theology, **Jesus Christ** is regarded as the most central and ultimately the most important figure—often described as the “Prophet, Priest, and King” in the New Testament. While the Old Testament prophets such as Moses, Isaiah, and Jeremiah are highly revered for their role in preparing the way for the Messiah, Christianity teaches that Jesus fulfills and surpasses all prophetic tradition. He is seen as the fulfillment of the Old Testament prophecies, the one who brings the new covenant, and the ultimate revelation of God’s will to humanity. Thus, within Christian belief, Jesus is considered the paramount prophet and the focal point of faith.
